transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-20 16:00 PT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Recording: Fireflies auto-record
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood Product), Alex (Nova CTO), Priya (ML Platform), Daniel (SRE), Sophie (PM)

Summary: Quick demo of API + Console flows for JSON-mode output + tool/function integration. Walkthrough focused on operator-visible guardrails (schemas, required fields, fallback policies), runtime routing (hosted vs dedicated), and a proposed 1-week dedicated pilot to validate latency and cost. Security questions on VPC and KMS surfaced; agreed to share SOC2/compliance artifacts and pilot pricing.

Topics covered:
- JSON-mode and schema enforcement in Console and API
- Tool calling patterns and safe fallbacks (no-execution mode, validation before call)
- Runtime routing and autoscale considerations for Dedicated
- Observability: token-level costs, traces, and structured evals

00:00 - 00:22 Maya: Hey everyone thanks for making time. quick intro from our side, I'm Maya AE on Redwood quick 1 min round robin?
00:23 - 00:36 Alex: Alex here CTO at Nova Labs, we run inference pipelines for the data product team, excited to see JSON-mode and tool calls, we've got some safety constraints.
00:37 - 00:55 Priya: Priya, ML platform, we care about predictable latency, batching and cost, and being able to verify outputs against schema before we trigger downstream actions.
00:56 - 01:10 Ethan: hi team Ethan SE, I'll take most of the demo - we'll show an end-to-end: API request with schema, how the Console surfaces failures, and the guardrails for tool invocation.

01:12 - 02:05 Ethan: ok starting the Console — this is the "JSON Ops" playground, you can attach JSON schema or a proto like contract. here i upload a simple schema for a support-ticket creation flow, we specify required fields: customer_id, severity, summary. note: the runtime will validate on generation and if it can't produce valid JSON within N attempts we hit fallback.
02:06 - 02:28 Sophie: quick Q - can we have nested required objects? like user.contact.email?
02:29 - 02:45 Ethan: yeah you can, the schema supports nested objects and arrays; the Console visualizer will show which keys are missing and even a confidence estimate for each field (approx). the estimates come from model heuristics so they are not perfect.

02:46 - 04:10 Alex: what happens if the model hallucinates an email? we can't call our downstream ticketing tool with bad PII.
04:11 - 05:05 Ethan: good question — two-layer guardrail: 1) pre-call schema validation rejects responses that don't match; 2) for sensitive fields you can mark them as "no-call-unless-verified" which routes results to a verification lambda (or human) before execution. we demonstrate a no-exec simulation mode so you can see the payload without calling the tool.

05:06 - 06:40 Ethan: switching to API example — we'll run a POST to /v1/generate with mode: json, schema: {..} and tool_calls: ["create_ticket"], the payload shows a structured response plus a tool invocation block. if the schema validation fails, the API returns a 422 with the validation diff.
06:41 - 07:00 Daniel: is that 422 behavior configurable? for some services we prefer a best-effort fallback rather than failing the request entirely.
07:01 - 07:32 Ethan: yes, there's a policy flag on the route: fail_on_schema_mismatch = true/false. if false, the runtime will do a best-effort repair attempt (n retries) and then attach a validation note in the response, plus the option to route to a lower-cost model variant as fallback.

07:33 - 09:05 Ethan: now runtime routing — you can set a policy: prefer_dedicated, min_latency_slo, and cost_weight. on capacity shortage the router will degrade to a compatible variant (quantized) or route to hosted if permitted. for Nova you'd probably want Dedicated for predictable latency, plus a hosted fallback for burst.
09:06 - 09:40 Priya: ok about Dedicated — what's the lead time to provision a pool? and can we pin single model versions?
09:41 - 10:18 Rina: provisioning varies by region and GPU class — typically 3-7 days for capacity in our US-west pool, but we can spin a smaller dev pool in 24-48 hours. yes you can pin model versions and pin a rollout window for canary.

10:20 - 12:00 Ethan: demoing tool calling safety: here i configure a tool manifest with allowed endpoints and an allowlist for domains. we also show signed webhooks and a pre-exec hook that runs a validation script. I'll trigger a simulated create_ticket tool call — Console shows the invocation payload, the validation status, and a simulated response. note: transcription of some names may be off — sorry if that shows up in the recording.
12:01 - 13:22 Alex: for our compliance team we need audit logs tied to requests and who approved human overrides — is that in the Console?
13:23 - 14:05 Rina: yes audit logs are stored per-request with token-level cost, the user identity, and the decision trail. we integrate with your KMS for key usage logs and you can export to your SIEM.

14:06 - 15:40 Daniel: about network — we plan VPC egress restrictions, can Redwood run in our VPC or do we need a VPN?
15:41 - 16:30 Maya: two options: Redwood Private (managed control plane in your VPC) or Dedicated with VPC peering for private egress. for full air-gap you'd choose our on-prem package. we'll share a diagram in the follow-up.

16:31 - 20:00 Ethan: performance checklist — we'll show a quick benchmark: small prompt (128 tokens), model X quantized on p4-like hardware. median latency for single-req is ~85ms, p95 210ms in our Dedicated config; batching can push throughput up but increases tail latency. when we ran Nova-like prompts with prefix caching and continuous KV reuse we saw 3-4x cost reduction. caveat: numbers vary by model and sequence length.

20:01 - 21:30 Priya: is quantized variant always our fallback? we can't accept lowered quality on certain endpoints (billing ops).
21:31 - 22:10 Ethan: you can whitelist endpoints where fallbacks are allowed. for critical routes you can set strict quality SLOs that prevent fallback or force a human review path.

22:11 - 27:00 Ethan: now a deeper example: schema-based reranking + tool call orchestration. the model returns an array of candidate actions; the runtime runs a post-validation step and then an orchestration policy picks the top safe candidate and triggers the tool. i'll show a live demo where one candidate fails validation and is dropped — Console highlights why (missing required_id).
27:01 - 28:18 Sophie: can we add custom validators? e.g., check that a user ID exists in our store before calling the tool?
28:19 - 29:10 Ethan: yes custom validators are supported — you can write a small webhook that returns pass/fail and reason; the runtime calls it synchronously before tool execution. we showed an example webhook earlier in the deck.

29:11 - 33:00 Alex: ok security deep dive time - what about encryption at rest and KMS integration? where are keys stored for Dedicated?
33:01 - 34:20 Rina: keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM. for Dedicated we support BYOK for model weights and request encryption if needed; audit logs reference key IDs. we will send the SOC2 and ISO docs after the call.

34:21 - 39:00 Daniel: curious about observability — how granular are the traces? we need per-token cost and the ability to tie back a token trace to a specific model invocation and tool call for billing reconciliation.
39:01 - 40:10 Ethan: Console has token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and a trace view that links model response fragments to tool invocations. you can export traces to your tracing backend or S3.

40:11 - 45:00 Maya: pricing and pilot — given Nova's expected volume (est. 10M tokens/week) we recommend starting with a small Dedicated pilot (2-4 GPUs depending on concurrency) to validate latency. pilot includes 1 week of dedicated capacity, support from SE for tuning, and access to Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization. we'll share a tailored cost model.
45:01 - 46:30 Alex: what's the cancellation and data retention policy for the pilot?
46:31 - 47:10 Maya: pilot terms are flexible — data retention defaults to 30 days but can be shortened; for production you can opt into no retention or strict audit retention policies. we'll include options in the follow-up.

47:11 - 50:00 Ethan: demo wrap — quick walk through console UI to create a route: select model, attach schema, choose policy flags (fail_on_schema_mismatch, prefer_dedicated), and configure tool manifests. then i deployed a canary: 5% traffic to new model version. Canary metrics are visible live.
50:01 - 51:10 Sophie: Nice - last one: can we run synthetic evals against a test prompt set to detect regressions?
51:11 - 51:50 Rina: yes Redwood Optimize supports eval sets and alerts on quality regressions tied to a route. you can tie an eval to a rollout and block if metrics drop.
51:51 - 52:00 Maya: thanks everyone we'll follow up with the doc bundle and pilot proposal.
